html:
Gelb is a noncommissioned officer commanding a fusilier platoon composed almost entirely of stones. He is coarse and faultfinding: during Dietrich’s inspection, he shouts at a soldier for a stain on his uniform and promises ten lashes, until the lieutenant cancels the punishment. He knows his men: he calls the holy-fool stone Salvation and considers Killnot, who cannot kill, the platoon’s “most valuable soldier.”

The night of the escape (ch. 2–6)

In the morning, Dietrich finds Gelb in a hut: he has been nailed to the wall through his palms and feet, and his jaw is smashed. He is badly wounded but alive. Dietrich orders Salvation to remove the nails and bandage his wounds, but runs off himself at the sound of horses. By the end of the battle, Gelb is dead. Dietrich gives Major Klein a different account, claiming that he tried to carry the wounded man, while Klein suggests that Gelb was abandoned to die.

Escape (ch. 33)

In ch. 33, the rifleman Killnot from his platoon is revealed to be Red. Gelb himself does not appear in this chapter.
